{{Short description|Theorem in Riemannian geometry}}
In [[Riemannian geometry]], '''Cheng's eigenvalue comparison theorem''' states in general terms that when a domain is large, the first [[Dirichlet eigenvalue]] of its [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] is small.  This general characterization is not precise, in part because the notion of "size" of the domain must also account for its [[curvature]].<ref>{{harvnb|Chavel|1984|p=77}}</ref>  The theorem is due to {{harvtxt|Cheng|1975b}} by [[Shiu-Yuen Cheng]]. Using [[geodesic ball]]s, it can be generalized to certain tubular domains {{harv|Lee|1990}}.

==Theorem==
Let ''M'' be a [[Riemannian manifold]] with dimension ''n'', and let ''B''<sub>''M''</sub>(''p'',&nbsp;''r'') be a geodesic ball centered at ''p'' with radius ''r'' less than the [[injectivity radius]] of ''p''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''M''.  For each real number ''k'', let ''N''(''k'') denote the [[simply connected]] [[space form]] of dimension ''n'' and constant [[sectional curvature]] ''k''. Cheng's eigenvalue comparison theorem compares the first eigenvalue λ<sub>1</sub>(''B''<sub>''M''</sub>(''p'',&nbsp;''r'')) of the Dirichlet problem in ''B''<sub>''M''</sub>(''p'',&nbsp;''r'') with the first eigenvalue in ''B''<sub>''N''(''k'')</sub>(''r'') for suitable values of ''k''.  There are two parts to the theorem:

* Suppose that ''K''<sub>''M''</sub>, the [[sectional curvature]] of ''M'', satisfies
::<math>K_M\le k.</math>
:Then
::<math>\lambda_1\left(B_{N(k)}(r)\right) \le \lambda_1\left(B_M(p,r)\right).</math>

The second part is a comparison theorem for the [[Ricci curvature]] of ''M'':

* Suppose that the Ricci curvature of ''M'' satisfies, for every vector field ''X'',
::<math>\operatorname{Ric}(X,X) \ge k(n-1)|X|^2.</math>
:Then, with the same notation as above,
::<math>\lambda_1\left(B_{N(k)}(r)\right) \ge \lambda_1\left(B_M(p,r)\right).</math>

S.Y. Cheng used [[Barta's theorem]] to derive the eigenvalue comparison theorem. As a special case, if ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;−1 and inj(''p'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;∞, Cheng’s inequality becomes ''λ''<sup>*</sup>(''N'') ≥&nbsp;''λ''<sup>*</sup>(''H''<sup>&nbsp;''n''</sup>(−1)) which is [[McKean’s inequality]].<ref>{{harvnb|Chavel|1984|p=70}}</ref>
